prompt: Create one complete 16:9 handmade paper/card diorama thumbnail for a historical London cost-of-living investigation. Show a thick, physical cut-paper threshold dividing three clearly related eras in one continuous handcrafted scene: on left a necessities basket sits near a daily wage token, at center the same-sized basket sits farther beyond the token, and at right it sits closer again. Use a bold stepped line of paper day-markers that rises at the center and falls on the right; keep baskets and tokens comparable in scale so perspective does not falsely imply the historical difference. The first glance should register a reversal, not a smooth upward trend. Add exact large rounded paper lettering: ‘THE PRICE WENT UP’. Tactile layered edges, folds, fibers and contact shadows; no exact numeric chart, dates, modern currency, logos, glossy CGI, or claim that the 19th-century change has one cause. Thumbnail QA title context: ‘The Centuries When Necessities Took More Work’. At 320×180, threshold, central rise and short text must remain readable.
visual_intent: A material threshold dramatizes the non-linear movement in selected model estimates. Check that baskets and wage tokens stay comparable and that it does not imply a continuous trend or explain the later improvement causally.
